doc.title: Nancy Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: AIDS work and the causes she cares about
summary: She talks about the National Minority AIDS Council and her concern for high school girls.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: And even though this is jumping ahead a bit, most recently you were involved in the National Minority AIDS Council.
Yes. That’s necessary, and a lot is being done, thank God, finally, but it isn’t in the forefront the way it was. Everybody feels that because we have some medications and

whatnot, it’s not that big a problem. It should not be happening. It should not be being transmitted at this point. We’ve been – we’ve known it’s around long enough to understand that this is a dangerous situation, and we’re still getting so many people who are being infected. That distresses me. It really bothers me.
What have I missed here in the causes that you have championed over the years? What are the things that Nancy Wilson is passionate about?

The high schools. I’ve gone into just about every major high school system in L.A. I went into – and as I said, just being concerned about babies, young girls having babies out of wedlock, this whole welfare system that perpetuates the same thing, over and over. That bothers me quite a bit.
